Suncor Energy stock: Record cash flow funds higher payouts
sum: Suncor Energy said on November 3, 2026, that record third-quarter cash generation had enabled higher shareholder returns and a planned exit from non-core offshore assets. The figures and corporate updates were published by BOE Report from Suncor's release.

Adjusted funds from operations reached 6.705 billion Canadian dollars in the three months ended September 30, compared with 3.831 billion Canadian dollars a year earlier. Free funds flow rose to 5.196 billion Canadian dollars from 2.347 billion Canadian dollars. Net earnings increased to 3.814 billion Canadian dollars, or 3.27 Canadian dollars per share, from 1.619 billion Canadian dollars, or 1.34 Canadian dollars per share.

Suncor returned 2.048 billion Canadian dollars to shareholders during the quarter, including nearly 1.4 billion Canadian dollars through share repurchases and nearly 700 million Canadian dollars in dividends. The company said planned monthly buybacks rose to 750 million Canadian dollars from 500 million Canadian dollars beginning in October, with total 2026 repurchases projected at 5.5 billion Canadian dollars.

The board also approved a 10% increase in the quarterly dividend to 0.66 Canadian dollars per share after the quarter. Suncor said the decision reflected confidence in the earnings power and resilience of its integrated business. Net debt stood at 1.751 billion Canadian dollars at September 30, compared with 7.147 billion Canadian dollars a year earlier.

Suncor agreed to sell its 48% interest in Terra Nova, 40% interest in White Rose and 38.6% interest in West White Rose for 1.2 billion Canadian dollars, plus a possible contingent payment of up to 350 million Canadian dollars tied to future oil prices. The transaction has an effective date of July 1, 2026, and is expected to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, partner consents and other conditions.

The buyer will assume future investment commitments and liabilities associated with the assets, including a 500 million Canadian dollar regulatory well-compliance program at Terra Nova beginning in 2027 and estimated future abandonment and lease liabilities with a present value of 1.4 billion Canadian dollars.

Suncor Reports Tuesday: What Canadian Energy Investors Should Watch as Oil Hits a 1-Month High
sum: Oil prices have surged as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are keeping investors on edge. And if you’ve been following Canadian energy stocks lately, you’ve probably noticed how quickly changing oil prices can influence sentiment toward the sector. Suncor Energy (TSX: SU), which is scheduled to report its third-quarter results on Tuesday, November 3, is one energy stock I’m watching closely as its share price has already doubled over the last year.
So, is Suncor heading for another blockbuster earnings announcement? Not necessarily.

Investors should remember that the latest rally in crude prices could be temporary, so its effect on Suncor’s third-quarter results might not significantly affect its long-term growth outlook. That’s why, beyond the recent oil price surge, I’d be more interested in looking at how Suncor’s underlying business performed during the quarter and whether its financial fundamentals remain strong.
Let me explain what I’ll be watching when Suncor reports earnings on Tuesday and why Canadian energy investors should look beyond the latest profit figures.

In short, Suncor mainly focuses on operating oil sands, offshore assets, refineries, and Petro-Canada stations. Its shares currently trade close to $111 per share, giving it a $131 billion market cap and a 2.2% annualized dividend yield.

Suncor stock has gained 15% over the past month alone and 100% over the last year, leaving it just slightly below its all-time high. Record refining activity, stronger cash generation and rising buybacks have supported that rally.

In the second quarter, Suncor’s adjusted operating earnings surged 336% year-over-year (YoY) to $3.8 billion, mainly due to higher prices realized on upstream production and stronger refining margins. As a result, its net earnings rose 229% YoY to $3.7 billion, while adjusted funds from operations jumped 98% to $5.3 billion. Better cash generation and lower capital spending also helped free funds flow more than quadruple to a record $3.38 per share.

Canadian Natural Resources vs. Suncor: The Dividend Stock I’d Own Through 2026
sum: Fort McMurray had a soggy second quarter in 2026. Suncor Energy (TSX: SU) CEO Rich Kruger said rain and snowmelt were the highest in more than 30 years, running 50% above the 10-year average.

That weather impacted mining productivity across the region. Suncor said it cut output by an estimated 50,000 to 60,000 barrels per day. Canadian Natural Resources (TSX: CNQ) said its teams had to manage haul roads through the same conditions.
Both companies still posted strong cash flow and paid their shareholders. But one of them has a dividend story that is hard to beat.
Suncor CEO Rich Kruger opened his call with a joke about Noah's Ark. The rain stopped after 40 days in the Bible, he said. In Fort McMurray, it kept going all quarter.
Suncor estimated the weather cut production by 50,000 to 60,000 barrels per day even as upstream output came in at 761,000 barrels per day.

Further, the company posted adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) of $5.3 billion, or $4.52 per share. Its downstream business set a record at $2.3 billion, while the energy giant ended Q2 with a net debt of $4.5 billion.

Given a quarterly dividend of $0.60 per share, the payout ratio for the TSX dividend stock was less than 20%, allowing it to strengthen its balance sheet. Suncor pays shareholders an annual dividend of $2.40 per share, up from $0.52 per share in 2012.

items.t: Suncor Energy (NYSE:SU): An Undervalued Value Stock With Strong Financial Health
sum: SUNCOR ENERGY INC (NYSE:SU) is an integrated energy company that has surfaced through a Decent Value screen, a strategy designed for investors who want statistically cheap equities without abandoning financial quality. The screen prioritizes strong valuation while still requiring at least decent profitability, health, and growth. That mix matters because deep value without operational stability can deteriorate into a value trap, while quality without a reasonable entry price can leave little margin of safety. The company's current fundamental report places it in that intersection: cheap versus peers and the broad market, financially solid, adequately profitable, and supported by a mixed but improving growth outlook.

The Decent Value approach does not simply chase the lowest multiples. It looks for valuation support alongside balance-sheet resilience and enough earnings power to avoid the classic cyclical trap. For an integrated energy producer, that distinction is important. Commodity prices, refining spreads, and capital intensity can swing results sharply, so a low P/E alone is not sufficient evidence of a bargain. The screen instead asks whether the discount is paired with solvency, liquidity, and a business that can generate cash through the cycle.
The report assigns an overall fundamental rating of 6 out of 10, with the strongest scores in valuation and health and a more moderate score in growth and profitability. The key observations include:

- Valuation: A price-to-earnings ratio of 12.57, below the S&P 500 average of 24.97, and a forward P/E of 11.88 versus the index's 20.28. The stock is cheaper than roughly 69% of industry peers on trailing earnings and 72% on forward earnings. Enterprise value to EBITDA and price to free cash flow also compare favorably with the industry, while the low PEG ratio suggests growth is not fully reflected in the multiple.

- Health: An Altman-Z score of 2.99, debt to free cash flow of 1.42, debt to equity of 0.28, a current ratio of 1.65, and a quick ratio of 1.08. Those figures point to a balance sheet that can absorb energy-market volatility without immediate liquidity or solvency pressure.

sum: OTTAWA — Prime Minister Mark Carney has met with a number of business leaders across different sectors to discuss Canada's trade relationship with the U.S.
A statement from the Prime Minister's Office says the meeting covered recent developments on the file and the government's priorities to spur economic growth and investment in Canada.
The statement says attendees were also invited to share perspectives from their respective industries.
Twenty-three companies were identified as attendees, including RBC, Enbridge, Bell Canada and Bombardier.
The meeting comes as Carney also named Dominic Barton as chair of Invest in Canada, replacing outgoing CEO Laurel Broten, a former Ontario cabinet minister.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Aug. 31, 2026.

Enbridge vs. Suncor: The Dividend Pick I’d Own Through 2026
sum: Canada’s large-cap energy names aren’t just known for their outsized dividend yields or their generous and very consistent dividend growth trajectories; they’re serious value contenders.

And in a market environment where value is getting passed up in favour of growth with themes like AI pushing investors to take a chance in tech names, primarily because of the recent momentum behind the shares, I do think that the second half could be an opportunity for contrarians to take a step back and consider the names that much of the market isn’t all too impressed by, at least of late.
Even with geopolitical tensions picking up in recent sessions, it feels like another surge in oil prices beyond the US$100 mark is off the table, at least for now.

And while it’s impossible to predict the next move, whether it’s a peace deal that lasts or a worsening of the conflict that keeps the Strait of Hormuz closed for some while longer, I do think that the energy sector could be a great place to score steady passive income for those who can stomach the share price fluctuations that are sure to be a bit more elevated from here.
In any case, this piece will feature two of the TSX Index’s heaviest hitters in energy: pipeline firm Enbridge (TSX: ENB) and the slightly choppier (and possibly cheaper) Suncor Energy (TSX: SU).

You cannot go wrong with Enbridge, given the 5% yield and modest 26.1 times forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple. If you’ve been around TSX stocks for long enough, though, you’ll know that shares of ENB have certainly been a heck of a lot cheaper with a far more swollen dividend yield. Indeed, a P/E in the teens with a yield closer to 7% was possible to land with the pipeline juggernaut not all too long ago.

But just because it’s pricier to get in with less yield, I still view Enbridge as one of the better dividend payers in the market right now, especially if the hunt for yield becomes a bit more scarce. Indeed, it’s not like there’s a massive list of 5%-yielders to pick from anymore. And certainly, none of the comparable dividend payers come close when it comes to dividend growth prospects, at least in my opinion.

Is Suncor Energy (SU) Stock Undervalued Right Now?
sum: While the proven Zacks Rank places an emphasis on earnings estimates and estimate revisions to find strong stocks, we also know that investors tend to develop their own individual strategies. With this in mind, we are always looking at value, growth, and momentum trends to discover great companies.

Considering these trends, value investing is clearly one of the most preferred ways to find strong stocks in any type of market. Value investors use a variety of methods, including tried-and-true valuation metrics, to find these stocks.

Luckily, Zacks has developed its own Style Scores system in an effort to find stocks with specific traits. Value investors will be interested in the system's "Value" category. Stocks with both "A" grades in the Value category and high Zacks Ranks are among the strongest value stocks on the market right now.
One company to watch right now is Suncor Energy (SU). SU is currently sporting a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and an A for Value.

Investors should also recognize that SU has a P/B ratio of 1.57. The P/B ratio pits a stock's market value against its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. This company's current P/B looks solid when compared to its industry's average P/B of 2.12. Over the past 12 months, SU's P/B has been as high as 1.63 and as low as 1.25, with a median of 1.47.

Finally, investors should note that SU has a P/CF ratio of 5.57. This metric takes into account a company's operating cash flow and can be used to find stocks that are undervalued based on their solid cash outlook. SU's current P/CF looks attractive when compared to its industry's average P/CF of 7.18. Over the past 52 weeks, SU's P/CF has been as high as 5.77 and as low as 4.06, with a median of 4.85.

These are just a handful of the figures considered in Suncor Energy's great Value grade. Still, they help show that the stock is likely being undervalued at the moment. Add this to the strength of its earnings outlook, and we can clearly see that SU is an impressive value stock right now.

Suncor Stock vs. Enbridge Stock: Which Dividend Giant Is the Better Buy for 2026?
sum: Canadian investors simply can’t afford to ignore $140 billion.

That was the value of Canada’s crude oil exports in 2025, according to the Canada Energy Regulator, with about 90% of that crude heading to the United States. The same report said Canada exported 4.3 million barrels of oil per day (boe/d) last year.

So while investors often talk about banks, real estate, artificial intelligence (AI), and technology, energy remains one of Canada’s most important wealth engines. Statistics Canada adds another layer to the story. In December 2025, Canadian crude oil production hit 27.8 million cubic metres, the highest monthly level since the start of that data series in 2016.

That helps explain why Suncor Energy (TSX: SU) and Enbridge (TSX: ENB) remain two of the most watched dividend stocks on the TSX. Both benefit from Canada’s role as a major energy supplier, but do it in very different ways.

Suncor owns oil sands assets, refineries, and Petro-Canada retail stations. This makes it an integrated energy company. When oil prices are strong, refining margins improve, and operations run well, Suncor stock can generate a large amount of cash.

Its first-quarter 2026 results clearly showed that strength. Suncor stock generated more than $4 billion in adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) and $2.9 billion in free funds flow. It also reported record first-quarter upstream production of 875,000 boe/d and record first-quarter refining throughput of 498,000 boe/d.

Suncor stock also returned more than $1.5 billion to shareholders in the quarter through dividends and share repurchases. Its quarterly dividend sits at $0.60 per share, and the stock recently yielded about 3.1% on the TSX. If oil prices stay firm and Suncor stock keeps running its assets efficiently, investors could see dividend income, buybacks, and capital gains work together.
